questions.stem: Why does an orbiting spacecraft remain affected by Earth’s gravity?
options: Gravity vanishes immediately above the atmosphere.
Gravity continues to act at orbital altitude.
questions.explanation: Earth’s gravity remains significant in orbit and continuously bends the spacecraft’s trajectory.

questions.stem: What can a gravity-assist flyby change?
options: A spacecraft’s trajectory and velocity relative to the Sun
questions.explanation: A flyby exchanges a small amount of orbital energy and momentum with the encountered body, changing the spacecraft’s heliocentric motion.

questions.stem: Why must a pressurised spacecraft structure withstand stress?
options: Interior pressure differs from the surrounding vacuum.
Solar panels eliminate all external forces.
The hull is always at the same temperature.
questions.explanation: The difference between internal and external pressure loads the cabin structure.

questions.stem: Why may a spacecraft change temperature between sunlight and shadow?
options: Its exposure to incoming solar radiation changes.
Vacuum always holds every surface at one temperature.
questions.explanation: Sunlight, reflected radiation and the spacecraft’s own heat balance vary with its environment and orientation.

questions.stem: How does an exposed radiator mainly reject heat to space?
questions.explanation: In near vacuum, a radiator rejects heat mainly by thermal radiation.

questions.stem: What can a spacecraft fluid loop do?
options: Create breathable air from vacuum without equipment
Eliminate the need for electrical power
questions.explanation: A fluid loop transports thermal energy within a spacecraft, often toward a radiator.

questions.stem: What do solar panels supply to a spacecraft?
options: A shield that blocks all radiation
questions.explanation: Solar cells convert part of incident sunlight into electricity; output depends on illumination and other conditions.

questions.stem: Which task belongs to a crew life-support system?
options: Maintain breathable air and remove carbon dioxide
questions.explanation: Life support manages the cabin environment, including oxygen supply and carbon-dioxide removal.

questions.stem: Why is propellant planning important for a spacecraft?
options: Onboard propellant is a finite resource.
Propellant automatically regenerates after every manoeuvre.
Propellant is needed only to power solar panels.
Propellant cancels the need for guidance.
questions.explanation: Most spacecraft carry a limited propellant supply, so manoeuvres must be budgeted.

questions.stem: Why is the radiation environment considered in spacecraft design?
options: Energetic radiation can affect people and electronics.
Space radiation changes every material into oxygen.
Radiation exists only inside the atmosphere.
questions.explanation: Energetic particles and other radiation can damage electronics and create health risks, so protection and mission planning matter.
